en: Reinforcement learning from human feedback,
or RLHF, is another term that's important to
understand when talking about AI and large
language models.
Large language models can replicate certain
behaviors or a human thinking process. They
can replicate human judgment because if you
think about it,
your thought process, your decision-making,
is in the end just text generation.
You may not be saying it aloud, but you may
be reasoning about a problem by just
spitting out text in your brain. And large
language models can do that.
Now, to
replicate these thought processes and to
make decisions,
they need to be fine-tuned for that though,
because just from the raw internet training
data, there weren't necessarily too many
decision processes in that. Data. But of
course, you can replicate decision processes
with synthetic data in fine-tuning, for
example,
and you can
replicate thought processes and
make this— and decision-making.
And one extra step or one special form of
post-training and fine-tuning is
reinforcement learning from human feedback
fine-tuning.
Where you let a model analyze problems and
ask it to make decisions.
And then you have a judge,
a human, since it's from human feedback, who
grades that
decision or the quality of that decision
that was made. And that grade is fed back
into the training loop and the model gets
that feedback. And the weights of the model
are continuously adjusted until it makes
decisions that are good. According to the
human judge.
So it's a different form of fine-tuning
where you don't just give the model finished
examples which are used to update the
parameters, but where you instead ask the
model to work through problems and you then
have a judge grade those results and then
that grading influences how the parameters
are adjusted. It's a more flexible form of
fine-tuning, you could say.
